scenes.text: Your phone is quietly becoming an AI computer.
On-device AI runs the model on your phone's own chip, not only on a distant server.
Phones now include a neural processor, hardware built for the parallel math behind AI.
That can cut waiting, since some requests skip the network, and some features can work offline.
It can help privacy, since some data may stay on the device, but that depends on the app.
Now the limits. Phone models are much smaller than data-center models, so they're weaker at complex reasoning.
They also cost battery, memory and heat, and phones throttle themselves to stay safe.
So the realistic future is hybrid: quick, personal tasks on your phone, heavy work in the cloud.
Your phone isn't replacing the cloud. It's becoming part of it. Follow for more future tech.
